chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Farsi, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Hafs al-Basri, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

The Earth did not complain to her Lord, Exalted and Glorified, as she complains from three things: from forbidden blood shed upon her, or washing off after fornication, or sleeping on her before the sunrise.

key_terms.عَجِيج: Complaint or groaning of the Earth

ai.seo_question: What are the three things upon which the Earth complains to God?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) identifies three specific acts that cause the Earth to 'complain' to God: the shedding of forbidden blood (such as that of the Imams or innocents), ritual washing after fornication, and sleeping on the ground-sleeping before sunrise. This narration highlights the cosmic significance of earthly actions in Shia tradition, linking physical rituals and daily habits to spiritual accountability and the physical creation's witness on the Day of Judgment.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-160 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn abil-Hassan al-Farsi , on the authority of Suleiman ibn Hafs al-Basry, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “
The three worst things of which the Earth has complained of to God are: undue blood that is shed on it; the washing off after fornication, and sleeping on it (after praying) before the sun rise.”
